The stack in one breath

STPi hunts country-specific sources (keys and availability vary) twice a day, Monday–Saturday across South Africa, Zimbabwe and Zambia,
scores every ad against the candidate's real profile, drafts a tailored cover letter
and a country-formatted CV as PDFs, and posts ONE card to your dashboard. You tap
approve — it sends from your mailbox, signed as the candidate, and the employer's reply reaches
the candidate and you (STPi flags interview invites). You tap reject — the PDFs are
deleted on the spot. Nothing sends without you, nothing is invented, drafts die at
72 hours, and the whole thing hosts for $0 on GitHub Actions. The demo is free
forever: one candidate, no card — one candidate, five sends per UTC month, free forever, the exact
same build the paying tiers run. No fetch waits longer than 45 seconds, no provider
longer than 30, no run longer than 35 minutes — a hunt finishes or fails loudly, with
the log streaming the whole way.

House rules for everything we publish

1. The human is the hero. STPi is the tool. Never "our AI got her the job."
2. Lead with the card (the product) and the tap (the trust).
3. Show the 72 h purge and the 20/day cap unprompted — they answer the two fears.
4. The demo is free forever; say so in every CTA. Never call the demo a "free trial".
   (The separate HOSTED trial is 7 days, 1 candidate, 5 sends; call it "the 7-day hosted trial".)
5. No "revolutionise / game-changer / guaranteed interviews / bot."
6. Southern-African specifics (SAIPA, SARS eFiling, VAT201, NRC, EcoCash) signal we know the market.
7. One CTA per post: the demo link. A reply keyword is allowed as the secondary.
8. Numbers are dated. Refresh before posting; stale stats are lies.

Product, precisely

Sell what it does, not what AI does. This section is the source of truth for every claim elsewhere in the bible.

The loop, step by step

StepWhat happensSells because
1 · Hunt06:00/10:00/14:00/18:00 SAST Mon–Sat; 18 board integrations; public search only, no LinkedIn login"it never sleeps and never forgets a board"
2 · Filterrules (location, exclusions, keyword) then a zero-cost pre-score (seniority, country, years) — throws out ~85% before any AI spend"your API bill stays in cents"
3 · Score + draftONE LLM call per shortlisted ad: relevance 0–1, one-sentence reason, letter, tailored CV. Hard-forbidden from inventing anything"it can't lie — check the letter against the CV"
4 · Rendercountry-formatted PDFs: cv_za (ID/EE/licence), cv_zw, cv_zm + cover letter; company names de-shouted ("SINOGY POWER PTY LTD" → title case)"it knows what a ZA CV looks like"
5 · CardWeb dashboard (primary) or Telegram (secondary): title, company, match %, reason, link, both PDFs, ✅/❌"your whole pipeline fits on one page"
6 · Tap✅ sends via SMTP from the operator's mailbox, signed "Candidate (via your brand)" (20/candidate/day, 150/mailbox/day; reply-to candidate + operator). Replies are spotted read-only and flagged in #activity: interview, question, no, bounce. ❌ deletes PDFs. Signed links expire with the PDFs"nothing sends without you"
7 · PurgePDFs deleted on send/reject and purged at 72 h; the letter text lives in the DB only while a tap is pending, is NULLed the moment you decide, and untouched drafts expire after 14 days; settled rows expire at 60 days"active generated-content expiry is not universal erasure"

Guard-rails (say these unprompted)

• Nothing sends without a human tap — there is no auto mode, it does not exist.
• The writer may only reorder/rephrase the profile; inventing is hard-forbidden.
• Four CV designs (classic · indigo · emerald · sunset), chosen PER CANDIDATE — the coach picks
  the look, the letter stays business-plain, every design ATS-parseable.
• 20 sends / candidate / day and 150 / mailbox / day — the operator's mailbox reputation is sacred.
• Replies: Reply-To = candidate + operator; each hunt reads the mailbox read-only and posts
  interview invites, questions, no's and bounces to #activity. Monthly report on the 1st.
• PDFs: deleted on send/reject, purged at 72 h. Untouched drafts expire after 14 days.
• Store: job metadata + status, plus the pending draft — text NULLed and PDFs unlinked the
  moment of approve/reject; settled rows expire at 60 days. Candidate = one YAML = right to
  erasure; tenant = one file = rm.
• No LinkedIn login, no profile scraping — public job search only.
• Gmail = one app password: SMTP to send, IMAP read-only for reply alerts; no Google Cloud project, no OAuth, no consent screen.
• Hosting default = two GitHub Actions workflows; $0, no card, nothing to sleep.
• Hard time budgets everywhere: 45 s per URL total, 30 s per LLM provider then instant
  failover, 35 min per run — a stalled hunt is a logged failure, never a silent freeze.
• Candidate documents never enter the git state branch: state is metadata-only by code,
  and the runner untracks any stray PDF before every snapshot.
• --dry never marks a job seen: testing cannot eat tomorrow's leads.
• Demo caps are code, not policy — an atomic ledger in the same wheel; at the cap the
  approve button itself pitches the upgrade.

Architecture one-liner (for technical buyers)

hunters (18) → rule filter → zero-cost pre-score → ONE score+draft LLM call →
Jinja2/WeasyPrint PDFs (ZA/ZW/ZM) → SQLite (metadata only) → approval card (web dashboard) →
signed approve/reject → SMTP send from the operator's mailbox → purge → reply watch (IMAP, read-only).
The application ledger lives on a private git branch as a single squashed snapshot commit;
candidate documents never enter git.
Secrets Fernet-encrypted at rest. Every network call runs under a wall-clock budget
(45 s URL / 30 s provider / 35 min run) with unbuffered streaming logs. Optional bare
operator dashboard gated by STPI_ADMIN_TOKEN; hosted-customer control center on a
Cloudflare Worker + D1 (free tier, opt-in); self-hosted licence via Cloudflare Worker
(read-only on expiry, never bricked).

Market & ICP

Why now

• Job search in ZA/ZW/ZM is still board-by-board, manual, and tab-heavy — the pain is
  weekly and universal.
• Coaches charge per bundle (R600–R1500) but eat hours producing them — margin is time.
• AI made drafting cheap, but trust did not follow: the market rewards the tool that
  keeps a human in the loop and can prove it.
• Hosting collapsed to $0 (GitHub Actions), so a full pipeline can be given away free —
  the demo IS the marketing budget.
• Payments localised: Whop cards/crypto, Lightning via coinos, Mukuru grants — the rails
  the region actually uses.

Pain economics (the maths you say out loud)

One coach, three candidates, six boards, four hunts a week ≈ 8–12 h of hunt-and-rewrite.
At a conservative R350/h of billable coaching time, that's R3 000–R4 200 of unsellable
hours a month. Solo is $306 a month (about R4,999) — bill it to the client whose three candidates it
runs, and it's a line item, not an expense. The demo is R0. The maths sells itself — say it plainly.

What each purchase does (so you can promise it)

Rationale (so every seller believes the numbers)

• Demo R0 forever is the marketing budget: ~1 hunt-minute/day on Actions, cents of LLM on
  the customer's own key. Upgrade trigger is natural — the second candidate.
• Solo $306/mo (about R4,999) ≈ 3–5 CV-and-letter bundles at prevailing coach rates (R600–R1500) plus the
  8–12 h of hunt-and-rewrite time it deletes. The memo's month-1 maths: 4 × $306 (about R4,999) ≈ R20k.
• Annual prepay is the close that funds the build: $2,754 / $5,517 / $8,280 (25% off), one bank-wire
  payment on Whop — one Solo deal ≈ $2.75k, cash now beats MRR while the runway is $0. Offer it everywhere;
  never discount monthly.
• Rands remove the "dollars?" objection for ZA buyers: the same plans bill R4,999 / R9,999 / R15,000.
• Studio $613 (about R9,999) is priced for throughput: a studio earns it back in one extra order a week;
  white-label PDFs are the wedge (studios sell their brand).
• Sovereign $920 (about R15,000) undercuts a junior recruiter-day and kills the two real agency
  objections: data residency and lock-in. Delivery is self-serve (licence + install steps by WhatsApp, ~15 minutes with Docker); install help is WhatsApp.
• Never discount monthly in public; annual is the only lever. Private discounts for
  universities, NGOs, cohorts of 10+.
• Never per-send pricing — it incentivises spam and contradicts the guard-rails story.

The complete library, embedded verbatim from copy/sales-scripts.md (2026-09-19) — every script below, nothing held back in the repo. Copy buttons work on all of them. The offer on the table is always the free demo.

Every script assumes the free demo is the offer on the table: anyone gets it, no card, no call required. The paid conversation only starts after they've seen a card land.

Voice rules (BRAND.md): plain, specific, the human is the hero, never "bot", never "guaranteed interviews". The word demo means free forever tier — 1 candidate, 5 sends a month — not a time-boxed trial.

1.3 Voicemail

1.4 Discovery questions (use in order, shut up after each)

1. "Walk me through one candidate's week with you right now — boards, letters, sends."
2. "How many hours of that is hunt-and-rewrite, honestly?"
3. "What happens when you're fully booked — which candidates get thin service?"
4. "If the hunt-and-rewrite vanished tomorrow, what would you do with those hours?"
*(this is the one that sells; let them say it)*
5. "Who approves what goes out today?" *(answer is always "me" — that's the product)*

about Solo at $306 a month (about R4,999) — three candidates on the same machine. Fair?"

6 · Persona scripts

Solo career coach

Pain: capacity. "You're the bottleneck — every extra candidate is an extra Sunday." Pitch: "The demo gives you one candidate on autopilot-with-a-brake. When card number four lands and you've only spent one tap on it, $306 (about R4,999) for three candidates is the easiest yes of your month."

CV-writing / job-search studio

Pain: margin on bundles. "You charge R600–R1500 per CV-and-letter bundle and eat hours writing them. STPi produces the bundle in minutes with your brand on the PDF (Studio tier). Your writers edit instead of type — you triple throughput at the same price."

University career centre

Pain: thousands of students, six staff. "Run the demo on one faculty's honours cohort. The card format is the report your dean wants: matches, reasons, approvals. Sovereign tier keeps every byte on your own box — your compliance office will love that sentence."

Outplacement firm

Pain: billable hours vs. outcomes. "Your consultants bill for judgement, not tab management. STPi frees the judgement hours; the audit trail (match %, approve timestamps) goes into your client reporting."

Recruiter moving into coaching

Pain: ATS muscle memory. "You know what an ATS is for — employers. This is the candidate-side desk. Same discipline, opposite direction."

NGO / workforce-development programme

Pain: donor reporting + scale. "Every approved send is a data point for your funders: who, where, match %, outcome. Demo one cohort; the reporting story writes your next grant."

7 · Objection scripts (short, repeatable)

"Does it apply by itself?" → "No. There is no auto mode. Every send is your tap — that's a design guarantee, not a setting. The demo will show you the ❌ working too."

"AI letters are generic." → "Open the sample. Second paragraph names the company and mirrors two real requirements. Now show me the letter they wrote at 11pm — same one, thirty employers. That's generic."

"My Gmail will get flagged." → "Sends go from your mailbox to real ads, human-approved, capped at 20 per candidate and 150 per mailbox a day. That's cleaner than most manual spraying — the cap is the feature. Tip: use a separate Gmail just for applications."

"It's expensive." → "The demo is R0 forever. Solo is $306/mo (about R4,999) — two or three bundled CV-and-letter sales at your prices. If STPi doesn't produce one bundle a month, cancel in the app, no email needed."

"I already use ChatGPT." → "Great — you've felt the magic and the maintenance. Who sweeps the boards at 06:00? Who purges the PDFs? Who keeps the three countries' CV formats current? STPi is the difference between a prompt and a pipeline."

"My candidates won't trust it." → "The employer gets a normal email signed by the candidate, 'Thandi Moyo (via your practice)', and their reply goes straight to the candidate as well as to you. The candidate sees their own letter in the card before it flies. The only new thing in their life is that Tuesday got shorter."

"We're an agency, data can't leave." → "Sovereign. Your box, your cloud. The licence is signed and checked offline, so nothing phones home; if it lapses the box goes read-only, never bricked. Data never leaves."

"Dollars? We pay in rands." → "Same plans in rands: R4,999, R9,999 or R15,000 a month, same Whop checkout."

"Can we pay once for the year?" → "Yes, 25% off: $2,754 for Solo, one bank transfer through Whop. Whop caps cards at $2,500, which is why annual goes by wire."

"Boards will block it." → "They try; we degrade gracefully. Each hunter fails alone — last run, one board 403'd and the other ten delivered. You never get a dead pipeline, just a shorter list that day."

"I don't have time to set it up." → "Ten minutes, and I stay on the call. Webhook, app password, one YAML. If we're not live in ten minutes I owe you a coffee voucher."

"What's the catch with free?" → "The demo is the marketing budget. One candidate free forever, five sends a month. Your second candidate is my invoice."

"Send me information." → "Better: the information is a working demo. Ten minutes on your phone, free forever. I'll send the link and stay available — you'll learn more from one card than any PDF I could attach."

"Who else uses it?" → "We're early — you'd be one of the first in {{country}}, and I'll say that plainly. What you get for that: my personal number, and pricing locked for a year."

FAQ

Does it apply automatically?

No. There is no auto mode. Every send is a human tap — a design guarantee, not a setting.

Will it invent experience?

No. The writer may only reorder/rephrase the profile. Check the sample CV against the sample letter, line by line.

Spam risk?

Your mailbox, real ads, human-approved, 20/candidate and 150/mailbox a day. The opposite of spray-and-pray.

Data?

Store = job metadata + status + the draft awaiting your tap; the tap deletes both the text and the PDFs, and settled rows expire after 60 days. Candidate documents never persist to the git state branch — the runner untracks stray PDFs before every snapshot (enforced since the 2026-09-19 hardening). Candidate file = one YAML = right to erasure.

Will I know if a candidate gets an interview?

Yes. Replies go to the candidate and to your mailbox; STPi reads your mailbox read-only and posts in #activity when an employer answers (interview invite, question, no, bounced address), and a monthly report counts interviews per candidate. Interviews arranged only by phone won't show.

Whose mailbox sends?

The operator's (one per practice; a separate Gmail just for applications is best). The From line reads "Thandi Moyo (via your practice)". Caps: 20 per candidate and 150 per mailbox a day.

LinkedIn?

No login, no scraping. Public job search only.

Boards?

22 boards supported, 17 on by default: Adzuna · Google for Jobs (JSearch) · PNet · CareerJunction · JobMail · Bizcommunity · VacancyMail · iHarareJobs · JobsZimbabwe · GoZambiaJobs · Impactpool · LinkedIn · Himalayas · Jobicy · Remotive, plus ReliefWeb (NGO/UN) once its API name is approved. Careers24 and UNjobs are supported but off by default (they block datacentre IPs). CVs: ZA/ZW/ZM formats.

Cost to run?

$0 default — GitHub Actions. Customer brings a free-tier LLM key + a Gmail app password. No cloud console, no card.

Why is the demo free forever?

Because the demo IS the marketing budget and the upgrade trigger is natural: your second candidate. "Free trial" implies a bill; "free forever" implies confidence.

What does upgrading unlock?

More candidates (3/15/unlimited), more sends, white-label PDFs (Studio), self-hosting (Sovereign). The pipeline itself is identical at R0.

Can I pay in rands?

Yes. Every plan has a rand checkout on Whop: Solo R4,999, Studio R9,999, Sovereign R15,000 a month.

Can I pay yearly?

Yes, 25% off in one bank-wire payment on Whop: $2,754 / $5,517 / $8,280. Whop only takes cards up to $2,500, so annual goes by wire.

Where do I approve?

Hosted plans (trial, Solo, Studio): on your web dashboard. Self-hosted (demo pack, Sovereign): the web dashboard, Telegram, or a Discord webhook.

How does Sovereign arrive?

By WhatsApp: the signed licence, the docker pull line and the install guide arrive together; every renewal re-delivers a fresh licence. The image is public; the licence is the lock. WhatsApp +263 78 460 0904 is the backup.

Is there a trial?

Two front doors: the self-hosted demo is free forever (1 candidate, one candidate + five sends per UTC month, free forever); the 7-day hosted trial needs no install (1 candidate, 5 sends) and upgrades in place when they buy with the same email.

What if a board dies?

Hunters fail alone. The run logs "[hunter:x] 0 jobs" and the rest deliver. Coverage degrades gracefully.

Can it run unsupervised without getting stuck?

That's the 2026-09-19 hardening: every URL gets a 45 s total budget, every LLM provider 30 s of politeness before instant failover, every run a 35-minute cap — and logs stream live from the first second. A hung hunt is a logged failure, never a silent freeze.

Is the free demo a crippled app?

No fork, no watermarks — the identical wheel and the same country-specific sources (keys and availability apply). The ledger caps output at one candidate, five sends per UTC month, free forever; at the cap, the pipeline itself tells you what upgrading buys. Licence flips the flavour env; nothing else changes.

Unit economics (say it internally, not to buyers)

Demo cost ≈ 1 hunt-min/day (Actions) + cents of LLM on the CUSTOMER's key ≈ ~R2/mo.
Solo $306 (about R4,999) at even 5% demo→paid conversion = R250 per demo acquired ≈ one lunch out.
Churn killer: the pipeline accumulates seen-jobs history; leaving means starting blind.

Operating routine

One operator runs this alongside a client load of ten to twenty. Day one gets it going; the daily loop keeps it going. Every step cites its script — the tabs are the armory, this tab is the drill.

Day one — start here

  1. List 10 warm names — coaches, a CV studio, anyone you've helped with CVs. That's today's target, not a cold spreadsheet.
  2. §5 LinkedIn/WhatsApp DMs to all ten (Sales scripts tab — the 5-touch §3 sequence is already scheduled by the cadence table, §10).
  3. §1.2 opener for whoever replies — thirty seconds, then close them onto setup on the call (§1.5). You stay on the line while they run the guide. First card lands by the next hunt slot (06:00/10:00/14:00/18:00 SAST) — which is why “before 14:00” is your deadline line (§8).
  4. When someone says “I want this for everyone I have” → guide §12: confirm tier, take payment manually (never provision before money lands), copy a tenant YAML, flip their build off demo, ask for the day-3 screenshot.
  5. Keep a tally of conversations → installs → first-card-taps. That's the only dashboard you need at 10 conversations deep — template below.

The daily loop (SAST clock)

WhenDoWhy / source
06:00Nothing — the pipeline hunts on its own. cron 04/08/12/16 UTC; a dead board never kills a run
08:30Ninety-second card scan: approve, reject, answer any reply on the candidate's thread. Clear the queue before your first client session. the tap is the product; ignore = 72 h auto-purge
10:00–11:00Outreach block: five new conversations. Scripts §1 (phone) / §5 (DM) / §6 (per persona). Log every one in the tally. five focused > fifty sprayed
13:45Same-day installs: get today's yes onto the setup call before the 14:00 slot so the first card lands while the excitement is fresh. Then follow-ups due per the cadence table (§10): day 0+1h, 2, 5, 9; demo+3, +7. deadline close, §8 — honest, not fake scarcity
18:10Run health: the evening log in sixty seconds — per-board job counts, any 429, the breaker line, persist commit on the state branch. anomalies are rare and cheap to read; setup guide §11 is the decoder
before bedUpdate the tally; queue tomorrow's ten names. The pipeline must never run dry on either end. list decay is the real churn risk, not objection handling

Weekly and triggered

  • Monday: refresh every number you quote from the latest hunt logs — applications drafted/sent, boards delivering. A stale number is a small lie with a big trust cost.
  • Wednesday: read the week's rejects — the pattern goes into candidate keywords; the matcher learns your clients' taste through the ❌ button.
  • demo+30 prospects: renewal courtesy line (cadence §10) — a check-in, not a pitch.
  • Any “yes, for everyone I have”: setup.html §12, in order, every time — money lands first, always.

The tally (the only dashboard)

date | who | channel | stage | next touch | notes
2026-09-19 | Rudo M. (coach, Harare) | WhatsApp | installed, awaiting 1st card | demo+3 question | picked sunset CV
stages: listed → DM'd → talked → installed → first card → tapping → asked to pay → paid
one line per person, updated in the before-bed slot; the funnel's health is the
distance people stall at — stalls at “installed, no card” means a setup problem,
stalls at “talked, no install” means a pitch problem. Fix the stage, not the people.

Standing rules

  • Quote no number older than three days; numbers come from hunt logs, never from memory.
  • Never provision before money lands — the manual rails are fully honoured until checkout goes live; demo-first is the promise, so nothing is ever rushed at a prospect.
  • Any reply resets the cadence to a conversation — scripts are openers, not cages.
  • Never say “guaranteed” of anything an employer decides. Guard-rails tab has the sentence to use instead.

"Pipeline" / "copilot" with buyers. Southern-African specifics welcome (SAIPA, SARS eFiling,
VAT201, NRC, EcoCash). Demo persona only — never screenshot a real candidate.

Engine truth — the product without adjectives

Exact state as of the 2026-09-23 live check. Say these sentences to buyers instead of guessing; every line is backed by the repo, not by marketing memory.

The wheel, fact-checked

ClaimTruth
"22 boards, 17 by default"Accurate count from the code: 22 boards registered, 17 of them used by default. Not every board returns ads on every run (some block datacentre IPs or go quiet), so say "coverage degrades gracefully", never "all boards live".
"Human approval before sending"TRUE — nothing sends without a human tap. That gate is the product.
"No auto-apply"TRUE — there is no auto-send code path anywhere in the pipeline.
"72 h data purge"TRUE for rendered PDFs (pdf_ttl_hours: 72). Candidate YAML stays until the file is deleted (delete = erasure).
"Runs on $0"TRUE for the operator (GitHub Actions + Cloudflare free tiers; no server, no card). The only consumable is LLM tokens, keyed to the customer where possible.

Guardrails that exist in code (say these unprompted)

  • Daily send cap — 20 sends/candidate/day, hard-gated in the engine.
  • Demo caps — one candidate, five deliveries per UTC month, free forever, counted by an atomic ledger.
  • Seen-skip — a job already applied to is never re-queued (pipeline.py:67).
  • Freshness bias — newest postings first; the loop assumes the first 72 hours win the reply.

The pipeline, end to end

One loop, six steps, twice a day, Monday–Saturday. The buyer sees the card; this is what happens underneath — and the exact places where a human is load-bearing.

  1. Hunt — cron 0 4,8,12,16 * * 1-6 UTC (06:00/10:00/14:00/18:00 SAST, Mon–Sat). Each board scraper runs and fails alone: a dead board logs [hunter:x] 0 jobs and never kills the run.
  2. Pre-score — free rule/domain/seniority/country filters before any LLM spend. Zero-cost triage is the margin.
  3. Match & draft — the LLM scores each role against the candidate's truth file and drafts a tailored letter. Groq 429s auto-failover to Gemini.
  4. Render — country-formatted PDFs (cv_za with ID/EE/licence, cv_zw, cv_zm) plus cover letters.
  5. Approve — the card lands on your web dashboard with ✅/❌ (Telegram and Discord webhook notifications optional); the human tap is the only trigger for a send.
  6. Send — SMTP from the customer's own mailbox; results persist to the stpi-state branch and rendered PDFs purge after 72 h.

Nothing between draft and send is automatic. That single human gate is what we sell — and what the press copy already says.

House rules for everything we publish

  • R0 demo is the front door, always. Paid tiers are quoted in US dollars with the rand figure as "about": $306 (about R4,999) / $613 (about R9,999) / $920 (about R15,000) — and say buyers can pay in rands (R4,999 / R9,999 / R15,000 on Whop). Annual = "one bank-wire payment, 25% off".
  • Every posted number cites a hunt-log date; numbers older than three days get refreshed or removed.
  • No "guaranteed", no "AI-powered future", no auto-apply promises. (See Brand → voice.)
  • Process over promises: "coverage, drafts, approval, retention" — never placements.

Daily operations — run the business, not just the product

Practical, $0, and it does not turn you into an operator-slave: each loop gets cheaper per customer as onboarding self-serves.

The daily loop (SAST clock)

  • 06:00 — nothing; the pipeline hunts on its own.
  • 08:30 — 90-second card scan: approve, reject, answer replies. Clear the queue before client sessions.
  • 10:00–11:00 — one outreach block: five new conversations, each logged in the tally.
  • 13:45 — get today's yes onto the setup call before 14:00 so the first card lands while the excitement is fresh.
  • 18:10 — 60-second run health: per-board counts, any 429, the breaker line, commit.
  • before bed — update the tally; queue tomorrow's ten names. Never let either end run dry.

Money — unit economics and the $0 rails

Internal. Do not recite to buyers unless they ask how the numbers work.

Unit economics

MetricValue
Hard cost per demo customer / month≈ R2 (hunting + the customer's own LLM key)
Demo → paid conversion assumption~5% (conservative)
Cost per customer at 5% conversion≈ R250 acquired — one lunch out
Churn moatthe accumulating seen-jobs history — leaving means starting blind

Payment rails (all live, all $0 to run)

  • Whop — one-tap checkout, subscriptions, 30%/12mo affiliate programme. (Plans charge $306 / $613 / $920 every 30 days, or R4,999 / R9,999 / R15,000 in rands; annual is a one-time bank-wire plan: $2,754 / $5,517 / $8,280. stpi's press health step alerts if any drift.)
  • Lightning — coinos invoice, payer puts name+tier in the note; manual grant on settle.
  • Sovereign licences — signed automatically by mint on every Whop payment (CA key held only in secrets); manual-rail Sovereign sales use stpi licence-issue.
  • Mukuru / EFT — manual grant via WhatsApp; ref = your tenant id. No public merchant API, by design.

Hard boundaries

  • No card at any step. Every rail is free-tier or manual.
  • No paid tooling — if it costs money, it does not get used.
  • No marketplace fees — free listings only.
  • No new infrastructure spend — hosting is already free.

Roadmap — truthful and dated

What we are actually working on, not a wish-list for investors.

Now

  • Service-first. Sell attributable placements per customer per month, not software seats.
  • Sovereign self-host is the trust story and now self-serve: pinned-CA STP1 licences delivered by WhatsApp, 7 days' grace after paid-until, read-only on expiry — never a bricked box. Image v1.0.0 is public.
  • Lead capture is live — the demo page arms a real card into the lead database, no email farming.

Next

  • First paying customers. Zero so far; the next 60 days are conversations and demos, not features.
  • Ask Whop to raise the $2,500 limit → card and rand annual plans.
  • Whop product-page FAQ items (dashboard only; text in whop/product_faq.md).
  • Rotate the Discord webhook and settle admin-token custody.
  • Unified DNC enforcement + email/social-only leads.
  • Self-serve onboarding — spin-up that does not need you on the call.

Legal & compliance (quick notes, not legal advice)

• POPIA/GDPR posture: metadata-only store, 72 h purge, YAML = erasure, no profile
  scraping, sends from the data subject's own mailbox with their approval. Say this
  plainly; it is a selling point AND the compliance story.
• Candidate consent: the candidate (or their coach with mandate) supplies the YAML and
  approves sends — consent is structural, not a checkbox.
• Employer-facing: applications are truthful (profile-sourced) and human-approved; no
  misrepresentation risk by design.
• Boards: public search only, polite rates, no login. If a board objects, that hunter is
  removed — coverage degrades, legality doesn't.
• Marketing claims: never promise outcomes (interviews/placements). Promise process:
  coverage, drafts, approval, retention.
• The 7-day hosted trial ends without billing (no card is taken); buying is a separate Whop checkout.
• The demo is a product tier, not a trial — say "free forever", never "free trial", to
  avoid auto-billing expectations and refund disputes.

copy/pitch.md 462 words

The one-screen pitch — the story every other asset borrows from

STPi — pitches & positioning

Official tagline (README): “Jobs found. Applications drafted. You tap approve. It sends.”

Elevator pitch (30 s)

STPi is a job-hunting copilot for career coaches in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Zambia. It sweeps country-specific sources (keys and availability vary) on a schedule — PNet, CareerJunction, JobMail, VacancyMail, iHarareJobs, GoZambiaJobs and more — matches every ad against your candidate's real profile, scores the fit, then drafts a tailored cover letter and a country-formatted CV as PDFs. The whole thing lands in your Discord as a single card with a ✅ and a ❌. Tap approve and it sends the application from your mailbox, signed as the candidate. When the employer answers, the reply reaches the candidate and you, and STPi flags interview invites. Nothing ever goes out without your tap.

One-liner (15 s)

STPi finds the jobs, drafts the application, and waits for your tap. You stay the professional in the loop; STPi does the forty-tabs part.

Tweet-length

Your candidates aren't losing to better candidates. They're losing to the 40 open tabs. STPi hunts, drafts, and asks before it sends.

Positioning statement

For career coaches, outplacement teams and job-search mentors in ZA / ZW / ZM who lose billable hours to board-by-board searching and letter rewriting, STPi is a human-in-the-loop application pipeline that turns a private Discord channel into a deal-flow desk for job applications. Unlike CV mass-mailers and AI “apply for me” bots, STPi never sends anything without approval, never invents a word of experience, and deletes its own work product after 72 hours — so you scale your judgement instead of outsourcing it.

Stat block (verified, 2026-09-17, from production logs)

  • 18 board integrations across ZA · ZW · ZM · remote; 11 returned live results on the latest run
  • 41 drafted applications sitting in one Discord-linked pipeline, each with CV + letter PDFs
  • ONE LLM call per job: score + letter + tailored CV (≈3× cheaper than score-then-draft)
  • 0 auto-sends by design — every application is a human tap
  • PDFs purged at 72 h; deleted the moment you send or reject
  • $0 hosting: two GitHub Actions workflows, no server, no credit card
  • 20 sends/day/candidate and 150/day/mailbox hard caps to protect your mailbox's reputation
  • Reply alerts: interview invites, questions, no's and bounces flagged in Discord; monthly interview report

Don't say

  • “AI applies for you” (we don't — a human approves every send; saying otherwise is false and invites Gmail abuse questions)
  • “guaranteed interviews” (no such thing; we sell hours saved and coverage, not outcomes)
  • “scrapes LinkedIn” (we don't log in or scrape profiles; public job search only)
  • “unlimited applications” (we deliberately cap volume; quality-over-spam is the pitch)

6 · Persona scripts

Solo career coach

Pain: capacity. "You're the bottleneck — every extra candidate is an extra Sunday." Pitch: "The demo gives you one candidate on autopilot-with-a-brake. When card number four lands and you've only spent one tap on it, $306 (about R4,999) for three candidates is the easiest yes of your month."

CV-writing / job-search studio

Pain: margin on bundles. "You charge R600–R1500 per CV-and-letter bundle and eat hours writing them. STPi produces the bundle in minutes with your brand on the PDF (Studio tier). Your writers edit instead of type — you triple throughput at the same price."

University career centre

Pain: thousands of students, six staff. "Run the demo on one faculty's honours cohort. The card format is the report your dean wants: matches, reasons, approvals. Sovereign tier keeps every byte on your own box — your compliance office will love that sentence."

Outplacement firm

Pain: billable hours vs. outcomes. "Your consultants bill for judgement, not tab management. STPi frees the judgement hours; the audit trail (match %, approve timestamps) goes into your client reporting."

Recruiter moving into coaching

Pain: ATS muscle memory. "You know what an ATS is for — employers. This is the candidate-side desk. Same discipline, opposite direction."

NGO / workforce-development programme

Pain: donor reporting + scale. "Every approved send is a data point for your funders: who, where, match %, outcome. Demo one cohort; the reporting story writes your next grant."

7 · Objection scripts (short, repeatable)

"Does it apply by itself?" → "No. There is no auto mode. Every send is your tap — that's a design guarantee, not a setting. The demo will show you the ❌ working too."

"AI letters are generic." → "Open the sample. Second paragraph names the company and mirrors two real requirements. Now show me the letter they wrote at 11pm — same one, thirty employers. That's generic."

"My Gmail will get flagged." → "Sends go from your mailbox to real ads, human-approved, capped at 20 per candidate and 150 per mailbox a day. That's cleaner than most manual spraying — the cap is the feature."

"It's expensive." → "The demo is R0 forever. Solo is $306/mo (about R4,999) — two or three bundled CV-and-letter sale at your prices. If STPi doesn't produce one bundle a month, cancel in the app, no email needed."

"I already use ChatGPT." → "Great — you've felt the magic and the maintenance. Who sweeps the boards at 06:00? Who purges the PDFs? Who keeps the three countries' CV formats current? STPi is the difference between a prompt and a pipeline."

"My candidates won't trust it." → "The employer gets a normal email signed by the candidate, and the reply goes straight to them as well as you. The candidate sees their own letter in the card before it flies. The only new thing in their life is that Tuesday got shorter."

"We're an agency, data can't leave." → "Sovereign. Your box, your cloud, licence checked daily, read-only on expiry, never bricked. Data never leaves."

"Boards will block it." → "They try; we degrade gracefully. Each hunter fails alone — last run, one board 403'd and the other ten delivered. You never get a dead pipeline, just a shorter list that day."

"I don't have time to set it up." → "Ten minutes, and I stay on the call. Webhook, app password, one YAML. If we're not live in ten minutes I owe you a coffee voucher."

"What's the catch with free?" → "The demo is the marketing budget. One candidate free forever, five sends a month. Your second candidate is my invoice."

"Send me information." → "Better: the information is a working demo. Ten minutes on your phone, free forever. I'll send the link and stay available — you'll learn more from one card than any PDF I could attach."

"Who else uses it?" → "We're early — you'd be one of the first in {{country}}, and I'll say that plainly. What you get for that: my personal number, and pricing locked for a year."

STPi — lifecycle email sequences

Customer = the coach (tenant owner). Tone: plain, specific, no exclamation inflation.

Subject: STPi is live for {{tenant}} — 3 clicks to first card

Hi {{name}},

Welcome. Your pipeline already has a home; it just needs three things from you:

1. DISCORD (2 min)
   In your server: #stpi → Edit Channel → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook.
   Paste the URL into your tenant.yaml under discord_webhook (I did this with you

2. GMAIL APP PASSWORD (2 min)

3. YOUR FIRST CANDIDATE (5 min)
   One YAML: name, country, location, keywords, exclusions. Copy the example —

copy/pricing.md 655 words

Pricing copy and rationale

STPi — pricing (decided 2026-09-17, founder-approved mandate)

Currency: US dollars, set to the rand value (owner decision 2026-09-27: Whop bills USD; rand figures are approximate at R16.31 per $1). ZA/ZW/ZM buyers can also pay sats via Lightning or Mukuru/EFT at the day's rate. Bill monthly via Whop in USD or in rands (ZAR plans R4,999 / R9,999 / R15,000, added 2026-09-27); annual = 25% off, one payment by bank wire on Whop (Whop refuses card/recurring plans above $2,500 on this account, so annual is a one-time 365-day plan: $2,754 / $5,517 / $8,280; no rand annual for the same reason); affiliates 30% recurring 12 months. Every Whop plan charges exactly its price on day one (no extra first-charge fee).

Tier USD/mo ≈ ZAR Candidates Sends Extras
Demo $0 forever R0 1 5/mo full pipeline, Discord card, PDFs, 72 h purge
Solo $306 R4,999 3 100/mo priority hunt slots; approve in Discord (web dashboard + Telegram when self-hosted)
Studio $613 R9,999 15 fair-use (20/day/candidate guard-rail) white-label PDFs, brand header
Sovereign $920 R15,000 unlimited guard-rail self-hosted Docker; signed licence + install steps delivered in the buyer's Discord (WhatsApp backup); data never leaves

Why these numbers

  • Demo R0/forever is the marketing budget. 1 candidate × 5 sends shows the whole loop (hunt → card → tap → send) without costing us anything: ~1 hunt-minute/day on Actions, cents of LLM on the customer's own key. The upgrade trigger is natural: the second candidate. "You upgrade when your bench asks" is the honest funnel.
  • Solo $306 (about R4,999) ≈ two-to-three bundled CV-and-letter sales at prevailing coach rates (R600–R1 500), plus the 8–12 h of hunt-and-rewrite it deletes. If STPi doesn't earn its keep the customer cancels in-app and is right to. Annual $2,754 (about R45,000, 25% off) is the prepay close — one deal ≈ six months of runway, cash now.
  • Studio $613 (about R9,999) is priced for throughput, not seats: a CV studio that triples writer output earns it back in one extra order a week. White-label is the wedge — studios sell their brand, so the PDF header carrying their logo is the feature they'll pay the jump for.
  • Sovereign $920 (about R15,000) undercuts one junior-recruiter-day and removes the two objections agencies actually have (data residency, vendor lock-in). Onboarding day included because self-host failures are support tickets; a guided day is cheaper.
  • Prices are USD at the rand value of the 2026-09-23 service-first memo tiers (owner decision 2026-09-27): Solo $306 / Studio $613 / Sovereign $920 monthly (about R4,999 / R9,999 / R15,000); annual 25% off. ZW/ZM buyers can pay sats via coinos or Mukuru/EFT at the day's rate. Billing is enforced fail-closed (stpi billing grant); the Whop webhook path exists in billing.py.
  • Affiliates 30% / 12 months because coaches talk to coaches; Whop runs it natively and 30% is the number that makes a coach mention you unprompted.

Lines to use verbatim

  • "The demo is free forever. You upgrade when your second candidate asks for it — that's the whole sales funnel."
  • "Solo is $306 a month (about R4,999) — two or three CV bundles at your rates, and the ten hours of typing is gone. If it doesn't earn its keep, cancel in the app, no retention call."
  • "Annual prepay is $2,754 (about R45,000) — three months free, one payment, provisioned same day."
  • "Sovereign costs less than a junior recruiter's Tuesday."

Never

  • Discount in public. Discount in private for: universities, NGOs, cohorts of ≥10 coaches.
  • "Cheap" as a selling point. The selling point is hours; the price is just not a barrier.
  • Per-send pricing. It incentivises spam and contradicts the 20/day guard-rail story.

copy/faq-objections.md 805 words

FAQ and objection handling, verbatim

STPi — FAQ & objection handling

FAQ

Does it apply automatically? No. Every application requires a human tap on ✅. This is a design guarantee, not a setting — there is no "auto" mode to turn on. STPi is a pipeline for your judgement.

Will the AI invent experience on the CV or letter? No. The writer prompt hard-forbids inventing qualifications, employers, dates or skills; it may only reorder and rephrase what is already on the profile. Ask for the sample CV next to the sample letter and check line by line.

Will I know if a candidate gets an interview? Yes. Employer replies go to the candidate and to your mailbox. STPi reads your mailbox (read-only) and posts in #activity when an employer answers — interview invite, question, no, or a bounced address — and a monthly report counts the interviews per candidate. Interviews arranged only by phone won't show; ask candidates to tell you those.

Will my (or my candidate's) Gmail get flagged as spam? Sends go out from your mailbox, to real ads, human-approved, with hard caps of 20 sends per candidate and 150 per mailbox a day. A separate Gmail just for applications is best. That is the opposite of spray-and-pray.

What happens to the data? The store keeps only {job_url, status, timestamp}. PDFs are deleted the moment a card is sent or rejected, and untouched drafts self-delete after 72 hours. A candidate file is a YAML — deleting the file is the right to erasure.

Does it need my LinkedIn or scrape my profile? No LinkedIn login, no profile scraping. Public job search only.

Which countries / boards? South Africa, Zimbabwe, Zambia, plus remote-first boards. 22 boards supported, 17 on by default, including Adzuna, Google for Jobs (JSearch), PNet, CareerJunction, JobMail, Bizcommunity, VacancyMail, iHarareJobs, JobsZimbabwe, GoZambiaJobs, Impactpool, LinkedIn jobs search, Himalayas, Jobicy and Remotive. CVs render to ZA, ZW and ZM conventions.

What does it cost to run? The default deployment is two GitHub Actions workflows on a private repo: $0, no card, no server to sleep. The customer brings their own free-tier LLM key and their own mailbox (a Gmail app password — no Google Cloud project, no OAuth).

What if a board blocks the runner or dies? Each hunter fails alone. The run reports "0 jobs" for that board and everything else continues. One dead scraper never kills a hunt.

I'm an agency — can we run our own? Yes: self-hosted mode on your own box, licence checked daily via a Cloudflare Worker. On expiry it goes read-only — never bricked, never deletes your data.

How do customers pay? Whop (card / PayPal / crypto, with affiliates), Lightning via coinos for ZW/ZM, or Mukuru / cash as a manual grant. No other payment rails.

How fast is onboarding? ~10 minutes: a Discord webhook, a Gmail app password, one candidate YAML.

Objections

"AI cover letters are generic." Show the sample letter. Second paragraph names the company and mirrors two concrete requirements; the facts trace back line-for-line to the CV. Generic is what they were writing at 11pm — same letter, thirty employers. STPi writes a different letter per ad because the match reason is per ad.

"Mass applications get everyone blacklisted." Agree with them — then contrast: 20/day cap, human approval on every send, signed by the candidate, to ads that passed a relevance threshold. "This isn't volume; it's coverage. Every send is still a decision."

"We already use an ATS / agency." An ATS is for employers; an agency is for sourcing. You're on the candidate's side. STPi is the candidate-side desk. If anything, it feeds your ATS with better inputs.

"My candidates won't trust a bot." The bot never talks to an employer. The employer receives a normal email signed by the candidate ("Thandi Moyo via your practice"), their reply reaches the candidate directly, and every send needed a human tap first. The candidate sees their own letter before it flies if they want to — the PDF is right there in the card.

"It'll look like spam to employers." It's one application, to one real advert, signed by the candidate, with their phone and signature. Read any of the samples aloud — it reads like a person because a person approved it.

"Why not just use ChatGPT myself?" You can — and then also maintain the board sweepers, the match scoring, the PDF renderers for three countries, the expiry logic, the approval channel, and the 4am cron. STPi is the difference between a prompt and a pipeline.

"What's the catch with $0 hosting?" No catch, just honesty: GitHub Actions free tier is 2,000 minutes on a private repo; hunts run ~5 minutes, 2×/day Mon–Sat ≈ 100 min/month. The customer's LLM key and mailbox are theirs. Your margin is the coaching, not the compute.

copy/demo-script.md 848 words

The 5-minute demo script and 45-second video shot list

STPi — demo scripts

Before the demo, have ready (5 min of prep): - [ ] your Discord open on #stpi with 2–3 real cards visible (or run one manually: Actions → hunt → Run workflow; ~5 min) - [ ] one card you can approve live (or a pre-recorded phone clip of the tap) - [ ] the sample CV + cover letter open (samples/ in this repo) - [ ] the pricing line you've decided (see pricing section on the hub)

The 5-minute demo

0:00 — the pain (30 s) "Show me your Tuesday. Six boards, forty tabs, the same letter rewritten per candidate. That's the job nobody bills for. Watch what mine looks like instead."

0:30 — the card (90 s) open Discord "This is it. One channel, one card per opportunity." Read it slowly, point at each line: - "The board and the role — this one came off CareerJunction at 90% match." - "The match reason is one human-readable sentence, not a score dump." - "Both PDFs are attached. Open the letter — see the second paragraph? It names the company and matches two real requirements. It's built from the candidate's actual bullets, and the system is forbidden from inventing anything." - "And the two buttons. Approve, reject. That's my whole interface."

2:00 — the tap (60 s) "Watch a real send." Tap ✅ → show the confirmation → "Sent from my mailbox, signed as the candidate. When the employer answers, it reaches the candidate and me, and STPi pings me if it's an interview. The employer gets a normal human email. Now reject one." Tap ❌ → "Deleted. The PDFs are gone the moment you decide. Untouched cards self-destruct after 72 hours."

3:00 — the three fears (60 s) — answer before they ask: 1. "Does it apply by itself? No. Every send is your tap. It's a pipeline for your judgement, not a replacement for it." 2. "Will it invent things? It can't — the writer only reorders and rephrases what's on the profile. Here's the sample CV next to the letter; check me." 3. "Spam risk? Sends go through my mailbox, capped at 20 per candidate and 150 a day, and every one is human-approved. That's cleaner than most manual spraying."

4:00 — the money (60 s) "No server. It runs on two GitHub Actions workflows on a private repo — $0, no card. You're not buying infrastructure; you're buying your Tuesdays back." State price. Close with the demo stack: "The demo is free forever — one candidate, five sends a month, no card. Solo is $306 a month (about R4,999) for three candidates when your bench asks for it. Set the demo up now while we're on the phone; a first card appears only when a suitable new job is found." Landing page (lead capture + download): https://getstpi.pages.dev/demo

The 15-minute deep dive (studio / agency buyers)

5-min demo above, then: - 6 min — coverage matrix: open the board list (ZA: Adzuna · Google for Jobs · PNet · CareerJunction · JobMail · Bizcommunity · LinkedIn · remote. ZW: VacancyMail · iHarareJobs · JobsZimbabwe. ZM: GoZambiaJobs). "22 boards supported, 17 on by default; some boards block datacentre IPs, the pipeline degrades board-by-board without ever stopping — one dead scraper never kills a run." - 8 min — economics: one LLM call per shortlisted job does score + letter + CV; rules and pre-scoring reject ~85% of ads for free before any AI spend. "Your API bill is in cents because triage is free and judgement is scarce." - 10 min — data posture: active generated-content expiry; store keeps {job_url, status, timestamp}; candidate YAML is the right to erasure (delete file = gone); no LinkedIn login. - 12 min — billing rails: Whop subscription, Lightning via coinos for ZW/ZM, Mukuru handled as a manual grant. "Your customers pay how they already pay." - 14 min — modes: hosted (you run it for your clients) vs self-hosted (an agency runs their own box, licence-checked daily, read-only on expiry, never bricked).

Second volume. Same rules as the first: the human is the hero, nothing sends without a tap, the demo is free forever, the 7-day hosted trial is called exactly that, one CTA per artifact, USD prices with the rand figure as "about". Every script ends in a question or a demo — never in applause.

A · University career centre (departmental, budget season)

Opener (in person or call). "Your office sees hundreds of CVs a year and maybe twelve get tailored per role. That's not a quality problem; it's an hours problem. I run a pipeline that reads the boards for you and drafts the tailoring pass overnight — your advisors keep the judgment, the machine does the reading. Can I show you one approval card?"

The honesty beat (use early, it disarms procurement). "Two things it will never do: send anything without one of your advisors tapping approve, and keep any CV longer than the decision needs. If those two are deal breakers in the other direction, tell me now and save us both a month."

The pilot framing. Solo is deliberately the size of one desk: 1 advisor, up to 3 candidates, one term. If one graduate placement this term traces to a 06:00 hunt nobody staffed, you have the business case for the institutional conversation — and that conversation is Sovereign, not "more Solos".

RFP line that gets repeated. "Data stays with you: Solo on our hosted rails keeps documents for at most 72 hours; Sovereign keeps everything on your own servers with a signed licence. Your counsel will ask exactly one question about data flow, and this is the one-sentence answer."

B · Outplacement firm (corporate RFP)

The door. "When you offboard fifty people, twelve get your A-team. What do the other thirty-eight get — a PDF and good luck?"

The offer. STPi gives every affected employee their own hunt: boards swept on a schedule, fit scored against their real CV, tailored drafts behind the employee's own approval tap. Your firm reports hunt activity per cohort — the number your client's CFO actually wanted in the outplacement budget line.

The differentiator statement. "We are not a CV library and not a motivational webinar. We are the machine that makes thirty-eight people visible to the market on week one instead of month three."

Close. "Send me your next cohort size and country split; I'll send back a one-page coverage plan priced per seat — and one free demo seat you can run on your own machine this week to check my arithmetic."

C · NGO / workforce-development programme

The door. "Your funding report says 'beneficiaries placed'. Your team says 'we can't read two hundred job ads a day'. Both are true; the gap between them is queue depth, and queue depth is what I sell."

Funding-frame. Studio at about R9,999 a month runs fifteen beneficiaries with the NGO's letterhead on every document. For donor reports: hunt volume, sends per beneficiary, interview flags — the pipeline produces the metrics the programme officer currently types by hand.

The trust paragraph. "Consent is built in, not announced: every beneficiary (or their case worker) taps approve before anything leaves, drafts purge in 72 hours, and we never store a database of your beneficiaries on our side — Sovereign exists precisely for programmes whose funders ask."

D · TVET college /skills centre (ZA-ZW-ZM corridor)

The door. "Your graduates are skilled and invisible. The adverts that fit them are on PNet, VacancyMail and iHarareJobs at 06:00; your placement officer sees them at 14:00, behind three hundred others."

The wedge. "$306 a month, about R4,999, runs three graduates through the same wheel paying agencies use. If one graduate signs in the first term, the college recovered the year cost in a single placement story — and you can quote the hunt log in your newsletter home."

Objection: 'our learners don't have laptops'. The operator does — one placement officer with a laptop and a WhatsApp group runs the whole cohort's queue from one Discord. Candidates never need Discord themselves: the intake link is a form, and approval taps belong to the officer.

E · HR consultancy moving into career services

The door. "You already write the CVs. What you don't have is the hunt — you sell polish and hope the client brings the adverts. Pipeline ownership is how polish becomes a retainer."

The pitch. Studio: fifteen candidates, white-label documents, your firm's name on everything the client opens. Your consultants keep client-facing judgment; the machine reads country-specific sources (keys and availability vary), every morning before your kettle boils.

The land-and-expand line. "Start with your three most senior retainer clients in Sovereign if counsel is involved — institutions pay for the data sentence: everything stays on your servers."

F · Universal rescue lines (when the room goes quiet)

  • "What's the honest bottleneck — finding roles, or paperwork at speed?" (If they say neither, ask who they placed last month and let silence work.)
  • "The demo is one candidate, free forever, on your own machine. If it embarrasses me I want to know by Friday."

copy/emotion-engine.md 1592 words

The Emotion Engine (2026-10-14): AFGR selling system — anger/fear/greed/relief sequence, buyer Diagnosis, question bank, 20-min call, red lines

STPi — the Emotion Engine (AFGR selling system)

Status: canonical selling layer, added 2026-10-14. Sits on top of pitch.md, sales-scripts.md, pricing.md, faq-objections.md — it does not replace them. Those files carry the facts. This file carries the order, voltage and timing that make the facts move a buyer.

House rules still govern every line below (BRAND.md): plain words, specific beats impressive, the human is the hero, never "bot", never "guaranteed interviews", never invent a number. Emotion here means revealing a true cost more vividly — never fabricating one. If a line needs a false claim to work, the line is wrong, not the prospect.

1 · Why facts alone don't close STPi deals

A coach can agree with every fact we have — selected public sources, one tap, 72-hour purge, $0 hosting — and still do nothing. Agreement is logical. Buying is emotional. The formula for every STPi conversation:

SALE = (EMOTION × LOGICAL PERMISSION) ÷ FRICTION
  • Emotion = why act, why now.
  • Logical permission = the numbers the buyer repeats to a partner, a principal, a spouse, or themselves at 02:00. (pricing.md lines, verbatim.)
  • Friction = setup effort, AI distrust, "will it invent things?", "will my mailbox get flagged?" (faq-objections.md exists to delete friction.)

STPi starts every deal with a double fear problem: the prospect fears the 06:00 queue (inaction) and fears an AI touching their candidates (action). Every call must grow the first fear and shrink the second:

FEAR OF DOING NOTHING  must beat  FEAR OF THE MACHINE
(missed ads, capped bench,        (invention, spam flags,
Sunday typing, candidates lost     loss of control,
to faster applicants)              embarrassment in front of clients)

The tap is our fear-of-action killer. Lead with it, demo it, close on it.

2 · The sequence: ANGER → FEAR → GREED → RELIEF

Never open with greed ("make more money!"). Never close on fear (it freezes). The order below is mechanical, not decorative.

Stage Job In STPi language it sounds like
ANGER — open Break indifference. Name the villain. "Your candidates aren't losing to better candidates. They're losing to faster ones — the ads are posted at 06:00, there are hundreds of applications in by lunch, and yours are still being typed."
FEAR — urgency Make waiting the risky option. "Every candidate you take on adds Sunday typing. So your income is capped by your typing speed. If nothing changes, where is that in 12 months?"
GREED — desire Make the win personal and possessed. "What would you do with those hours back — take on two more candidates, or take Fridays back? One placement fee covers months of this."
RELIEF — close Make acting feel safe and small. "Nothing sends without your tap. Setup is ten minutes, we stay on the call. The demo is free forever; you upgrade when your second candidate asks."

The enemy is never the prospect and never us. The enemy is: the 06:00 queue, the 40 open tabs, speed beating quality, portal deadlines, ghostwritten 11pm letters, and the admin that eats billable hours. Stand shoulder-to-shoulder against it.

3 · Diagnose the buyer in 3 minutes

Archetype Spot them by Lead emotion Greed currency
Solo coach at capacity "It's just me." Sighs about evenings/Sundays. Anger at typing → Relief Time back, bench growth without an assistant
CV/job-search studio Talks bundles, margins, throughput. Greed More bundles/week at the same price, their brand on the PDF
Boutique agency / recruiter Talks placements, clients, candidate-side vs ATS. Fear + Greed Candidate-side desk, audit trail for client reporting
Career centre / TVET / NGO Talks cohorts, officers, reports, funders. Fear (invisible graduates) → Relief Queue depth per officer, donor-ready numbers, data stays home (Sovereign)

One emotion dominates. Sell to that one; use the other two as pressure.

4 · The question bank (their words become your close)

Ask. Shut up. Write answers down verbatim — you will quote them at the close.

Anger (find the villain) 1. "Walk me through a candidate's week with you — boards, letters, sends. Which part would you never bill a client for?" 2. "Tell me about the last role your candidate should have landed. What actually happened?" 3. "When an employer gets hundreds of applications by lunch, where does a hand-typed one land in that queue?" 4. "What are you doing on Sundays that a machine should be doing?"

Fear (price the inaction, in their numbers) 5. "How many hours a week is hunt-and-rewrite, honestly? And what's an hour of your coaching worth?" 6. "What happens when you're fully booked — which candidates get the thin version of you?" 7. "If nothing changes for 12 months: better, same, or worse? Why?" 8. "When a candidate quietly stops paying you, what reason do they usually give themselves?"

Greed (build the possessed future) 9. "If the hunt-and-rewrite vanished tomorrow, what would you do with those hours first?" 10. "How many candidates are sitting on your bench right now without a pipeline? What is one placement — or one bundle — worth to you?" 11. "Are you trying to grow the bench, get your evenings back, or both?"

Relief / permission (delete friction early) 12. "If you tried this, what would need to be true for you to feel safe pressing approve the first time?" 13. "Who else would want a say before you paid for it?" (Surface the partner/principal now. Hand them one-pager-partner.md.)

5 · The 20-minute AFGR call

0–3   ANGER   Show their Tuesday back to them. Name the 06:00 queue. Get THEM
              to say the typing is the bottleneck (Q1–Q4).
3–7   FEAR    Build THEIR cost number: hours/week × their rate × 4.3 weeks.
              Then Q7. Let silence work. ("Worse" is the only honest answer.)
7–11  GREED   One placement / bundle value vs $306. Bench waiting (Q10).
              Future-pace one scene: "It's 06:10. The ad landed at 06:00.
              Your candidate's draft is already waiting for your tap."
11–17 DEMO    Three scenes only (see §6). No feature tour.
17–20 CLOSE   Relief stack: tap control → 10-minute setup → free demo →
              price vs one placement. Recap close in their words. Then SILENCE.

Recap close (use their verbatim answers):

"You said [anger, their words]. You said twelve months of the same means [fear, their words]. And the first thing you'd do with the hours back is [greed, their words]. The demo gives you that on one candidate, free forever, and nothing sends without your tap. Shall we set it up now while I'm on the line — a first card appears only when a suitable new job is found?"

6 · The demo is three emotional scenes, not a tour

  1. REVENGE (anger paid off, ~2 min). Open the approval surface (dashboard; Discord/Telegram where that's the tenant's surface). Show one card for a real-feeling match (demo persona only — never a real candidate). Read the match reason slowly. Open the letter: second paragraph, company named, two real requirements mirrored. "This is the letter that used to be typed at 23:00."
  2. NIGHTMARE AVOIDED (fear paid off, ~2 min). Show coverage: boards swept, the ~85% thrown out free by rules + pre-score, the send caps, the 72-hour purge. "This is what runs at 06:00 while you're asleep — and this is everything it refused to waste your attention on."
  3. JACKPOT (greed paid off, ~3 min). Their numbers, live: hours back per month, bench candidates now coverable, one placement/bundle vs the tier price. Then the tap: approve one, reject one, watch it delete. Invite them to check the letter against the CV line by line — "If it invented one fact, delete the demo and tell everyone." A prospect who tried to catch the machine inventing, and failed, has no fear-of-action left.

7 · Follow-up is emotional rotation, not "checking in"

One emotion per touch. Stop on any reply. Full scripts: sales-scripts-emotion.md §7, outreach sequences: cold-outreach-emotion-rotation.md.

When Emotion Beat
Same day Relief "Setup slot held. Ten minutes, I stay on the call. a first card when a suitable new job is found."
Day 2 Fear Their cost number, restated: "That's ±R[x]/month of typing at your rate."
Day 4 Greed Bench maths: waiting candidates × one placement/bundle value.
Day 7 (post-demo) Pride/Greed Their real counts: cards, taps, sends. "Your bench called." (Solo nudge.)
Day 10 Anger The enemy content: the 06:00 queue, speed beating quality. No ask.
Day 14 Loss/closure "Closing the file — keep the free demo either way. One word ('later') and I return next quarter."

8 · Red lines (non-negotiable)

  1. No invented competitor adoption, deadlines, slots or results. STPI's market is small; coaches talk to coaches. One exposed bluff ends the vertical.
  2. Their numbers, cut by them. If a deal only closes on inflated maths, it closes into a refund.
  3. Anger at the queue, the tabs, the typing — never shame at the coach.
  4. "Guaranteed interviews" is banned language (BRAND.md). We sell coverage, hours and judgement at scale. The tap is the trust.
  5. The 02:00 test: comfortable with their partner/principal hearing the call recording? If not, rewrite the line.

1 · Cold opener (coach on the line, 30 seconds)

and yours are still being typed at night. I run a pipeline that hunts selected public sources twice a day, Monday–Saturday, drafts the letter and CV from the candidate's real

I'm not asking for money. Take the free demo — one candidate, free forever —
and watch three cards land. If they're worse than your Tuesday, delete it.
Did I earn the right to send the link?"

per real match, and waits for your tap — nothing sends without you. Free
demo, one candidate, forever, no card: https://getstpi.pages.dev/demo

If the typing is your bottleneck I'll set it up with you on a 10-min call.
If not, sorry for the ping.

3 · Discovery — the four questions that do the selling

Ask in order. Shut up after each. Write answers verbatim.

  1. Anger: "Walk me through one candidate's week with you. Which part of that would you never bill a client for?"
  2. Fear: "How many hours a week is hunt-and-rewrite, honestly? At your rate, what's that a month? … And if nothing changes for 12 months — better, same, or worse?"
  3. Greed: "If that typing vanished tomorrow, what's the first thing you'd do with the hours? How many candidates are on your bench right now without a pipeline — and what's one placement (or one bundle) worth?"
  4. Relief: "What would need to be true for you to feel safe tapping approve the first time?"

If Q2 produces no heat, you have the wrong prospect or the wrong wound. Qualify out politely — an unemotional prospect does not buy on this ticket.

4 · The 20-minute video call (AFGR cut)

0–2   "Two promises: no deck, and you leave with the demo running whether
      you buy or not."
2–6   ANGER+FEAR. Their Tuesday, their hours, their number said back:
      "So ±{{N}} hours a week of hunt-and-rewrite — at your rate that's
      ±R{{X}} a month of typing." Then: "Twelve months of the same?"
6–9   GREED. "First thing you'd do with those hours?" Let them build the
      scene. Bench maths: {{bench}} candidates waiting × one placement.
9–15  THREE SCENES (emotion-engine.md §6): (1) the card + the letter that
      used to be typed at 23:00; (2) the 06:00 coverage, the ~85% thrown
      out free, caps + purge; (3) approve one, reject one, watch it delete.
      Invite them to audit the letter against the CV for one invented fact.
15–18 THREE FEARS, unprompted: no auto-send ("no auto mode exists"), no
      invention ("check me, line by line"), no spam flag (your mailbox,
      capped per candidate and per day; replies reach candidate + you).
18–20 RELIEF CLOSE. "Setup is ten minutes and I stay on the line. Demo is
      free forever on one candidate. Solo is $306 a month (about R4,999)
      for three when your bench asks — one placement covers months of it.
      Which candidate goes in first?"

5 · Closing lines (use their words)

Recap close (default):

"You said [anger quote]. You said a year of the same means [fear quote]. The first thing you'd do with the hours back is [greed quote]. The demo does exactly that on one candidate, free forever, nothing sends without your tap. Set it up now while we're talking?"

Identity close:

"The coaches who take this are the ones who decided their judgement is what clients pay for — not their typing. Which way are you leaning?"

Calendar close (relief):

"Hunts run 06:00 / 10:00 / 14:00 / 18:00. Ten minutes before 14:00 and your first card requires a suitable new job. I do the setup; you just answer three questions."

Then silence. The first person to speak after the ask loses.

6 · Objections are emotion deficits — diagnose, don't argue

They say What's missing Move
"It's expensive." Greed not yet bigger than price. Re-anchor, don't discount: "Against what? One bundle at your rates is R600–R1,500; one placement is more. Solo is $306 (about R4,999) — two or three bundles, and the ten hours of typing is gone. Your own number said the typing costs you ±R{{X}} a month."
"Let me think about it." No peak, or fear-of-action winning. Diagnose aloud: "Usually that's one of two things — it doesn't feel worth it yet, or it feels risky. Which is closer?" Fix that one. Leave with a dated step + the one-pager.
"Send me information." You informed instead of arousing. "Better: test it. Give me 60 seconds — I'll show you one card and you check the letter against the CV. If it invented anything, I'll send the PDF and leave you alone."
"AI will invent / embarrass me." Fear-of-action. Legitimate. Agree first. Then proof, not argument: sample CV vs letter, line by line. The tap. The 72-hour purge. "You approve like it's a new staff member's first week — it earns trust, it never assumes it."
"I need to ask my partner / principal." The veto is logical, the decision emotional. Equip them: cost vs one placement, who sets it up (us, 10 min), how to exit (cancel in Whop, two clicks, demo stays free). Send one-pager-partner.md. Book the follow-up before hanging up.
"I use ChatGPT already." They felt magic + maintenance. "Who sweeps the boards at 06:00? Who renders three countries' CV formats, purges the PDFs, keeps the caps? This is the difference between a prompt and a pipeline."
"Too busy to set up." Overwhelmed operator. Lead with relief. "That's exactly whose setup we do. Ten minutes, I stay on the call: webhook, app password, one candidate. Not live in ten, I owe you a coffee voucher."

7 · Post-demo emotional rotation (stop on any reply)

demo+1h  RELIEF (voice note if WhatsApp): "Your pipeline is on. First hunt
         06:00. All you do tomorrow is tap ✅ or ❌ — nothing can send
         without you."
demo+3d  PRIDE/GREED: "First cards landing? The reject button is the most
         important one this week — it teaches the matcher your taste."
demo+7d  GREED (their real counts): "Week one: {{cards}} cards, {{sends}}
         sends, ±{{hours}} hours you didn't type. How many candidates are
         on your bench without this? Solo puts two more on the same machine
         for $306 a month (about R4,999) — that's [less than one placement /
         two bundles]. One tap: [Solo checkout]."
demo+14d ANGER (no ask): "The boards posted at 06:00 again today. Yours were
         covered before you'd finished coffee. That's the whole product."
cancel/  LOSS (win-back, honest): "The boards kept running — PNet alone moves
win-back ±70 finance ads a week in Gauteng. Your files were never hostage:
         YAMLs, yours, waiting. Same free demo, no awkwardness: [link]."

Rule: every touch = one emotion + one next step. "Just checking in" is banned.

8 · What never to say (emotion edition)

  • Never invent a coach/agency "already using it" in their town. We're early and we say so plainly (sales-scripts.md §7) — early-adopter pride and a year of locked pricing are the honest version of envy.
  • Never promise interviews. Promise coverage, speed, hours, and the tap.
  • Never shame the coach's current process. Attack the queue, never the human.
  • Never close on fear. Fear opens the wallet's attention; greed + relief open the wallet.

copy/cold-outreach-emotion-rotation.md 789 words

Cold outreach — emotion rotation (2026-10-14): anger→fear→greed→relief→loss touches, persona swaps, reactivation

STPi — cold outreach: the emotion rotation

Companion to cold-outreach.md and cold-outreach-sequences-2.md. Those banks are organised by persona. This one is organised by emotion: five touches that deliberately rotate ANGER → FEAR → GREED → RELIEF → LOSS, so no prospect ever gets the same feeling twice — and never "just checking in".

Laws (all banks): one idea per touch, one CTA (the free demo), stop on any reply, WhatsApp before email for ZW/ZM, numbers only when dated and true, candidate applications require approval; researched STPi sales outreach stays automatic.

Before touch 1: earn the anger (15 minutes of research)

Do not send to a cold list. Send to evidence. Look for 2+ of:

  • Their site/socials promise "we apply for you" or personal service — speed is their public promise, and the 06:00 queue is quietly breaking it.
  • They post candidate-success content but nothing about volume or turnaround.
  • They're visibly a team of one to five (the typing bottleneck is structural).
  • They advertise CV/letter bundles (Studio margin maths will land).
  • They're hiring admin/consultants (the bench is already straining).

Write one true, specific opening line from what you found. Generic = deleted.

The rotation (solo coach / small practice — adapt the persona banks for studios, agencies, centres)

T1 · ANGER (day 0, WhatsApp or email) Subject: the 06:00 queue

{{name}} — the ads your candidates want were posted at 06:00. Hundreds of applications land by lunch; the hand-typed ones land tonight. Your candidates aren't losing to better candidates — they're losing to faster ones. I run STPi: it hunts selected public sources twice a day, Monday–Saturday, drafts the letter + CV from each candidate's real profile, and waits for your tap. Free demo, one candidate, forever, no card: getstpi.pages.dev/demo — worth 15 minutes, or should I close the file?

T2 · FEAR (day 3, one number, no pitch deck)

One number from coaches like you, then I'll stop: ±8 hours a week of hunt-and-rewrite is ±R15k a month of typing at coaching rates — and every new candidate makes it worse, not better. The demo shows what one candidate looks like with that typing removed: getstpi.pages.dev/demo

(Use the prospect's own number if they've ever given you one. Otherwise this illustrative frame must stay clearly generic — "from coaches like you" — and be cut entirely if you can't stand behind the arithmetic.)

T3 · GREED (day 6, the bench)

Different question: how many candidates are on your bench right now with no pipeline under them? Solo runs three on this machine for $306 a month (about R4,999) — one placement covers months of it. The demo is free forever, so the bench can judge the cards before you judge the price.

T4 · RELIEF (day 10, delete the risk)

The thing everyone asks first: "does it send by itself?" No — there's no auto mode. Every application is your tap; drafts delete themselves in 72 hours; you audit the letter against the CV before anything flies. That's why the demo is safe to just… take: getstpi.pages.dev/demo

T5 · LOSS (day 14, the break-up)

Closing the file: the boards will post at 06:00 tomorrow with or without us. If timing's the only issue, one word — "later" — and I come back next quarter with better manners. The free demo stays yours either way.

Persona swaps (change only the greed line)

  • Studio: greed = margin. "You charge R600–R1500 per CV-and-letter bundle and eat the typing. Studio puts your brand on the PDF and your writers back to editing: throughput up, price unchanged."
  • Agency / outplacement: fear = the 38 of 50 who get "a PDF and good luck"; greed = a hunt under every affected employee in week one, plus an audit trail their client CFO can read.
  • Career centre / TVET: anger = "graduates skilled and invisible"; greed = one officer running a cohort's queue; relief = Sovereign keeps every byte on their own box for the funders' question.
  • NGO: fear = "beneficiaries placed" (the report) vs "we can't read 200 ads a day" (the team). Greed = the pipeline writes the donor metrics.

Reactivation (dormant demo users, emotion cut)

R1 · ANGER at the caps (day 0): "Your demo queue froze at the caps — that freeze is the pitch: the machine wanted to keep hunting. Two minutes unfreezes it for a real candidate: [upgrade link]." R2 · LOSS (day 5): "Drafts expire; the boards don't. Want me to keep your seat, or shall the file close properly?" Stop completely after R2.
